搭配：vitiate a contract 使合同失效
etymology: viti-(瑕疵，错误) + -ate(动词后缀) = 搞坏，使有瑕疵而失效
sentence_en: A minor procedural error was enough to vitiate the entire arbitration process.
sentence_zh: 一个轻微的程序错误就足以使整个仲裁过程失效。

definition:
adj. 尖酸刻薄的，刻薄恶毒的


搭配：vitriolic attack 尖酸刻薄的攻击
etymology: vitriol(硫酸盐，刻薄言辞) + -ic(形容词后缀) = 像硫酸一样腐蚀人心的，刻薄的
sentence_en: The online debate quickly degenerated into a series of vitriolic personal attacks.
sentence_zh: 网络辩论很快堕落为一系列尖酸刻薄的人身攻击。

definition:
v. 痛骂，责骂，怒斥


搭配：vituperate against sb. 痛骂某人
etymology: vitup-(缺点，责备) + parare(准备) + -ate(动词后缀) = 严厉责骂
sentence_en: Frustrated by the poor performance, the coach began to vituprate the players during halftime.
sentence_zh: 由于表现糟糕而感到沮丧，教练在半场休息时开始怒斥球员。

definition:
adj. 活泼的，快活的，神采奕奕的（多指女性）


搭配：vivacious personality 活泼的个性
etymology: viv-(生命) + -acious(形容词后缀，多产、充满) = 充满生命活力的
sentence_en: Her vivacious personality made her the center of attention at every social gathering.
sentence_zh: 她活泼开朗的性格使她成为每次社交聚会上的焦点。

definition:
adj. 生动的，逼真的，鲜艳的


搭配：vivid memory 生动的记忆
etymology: viv-(生命) + -id(形容词后缀) = 充满生命力般鲜活的
sentence_en: The survivor gave a vivid description of the earthquake that shook the mountain village.
sentence_zh: 幸存者对震撼山村的那场地震进行了生动的描述。

definition:
adj. 直言不讳的，嗓音的；n. 声乐作品


搭配：be vocal about 坦诚直言
etymology: voc-(声音) + -al(形容词后缀) = 用声音表达的，直言的
sentence_en: Local residents have been extremely vocal in their opposition to the new highway construction.
sentence_zh: 当地居民一直直言不讳地表达他们对新建高速公路的反对。

definition:
adj. 喧嚷的，大声叫喊的，叫嚣的


搭配：vociferous demand 强烈叫喊的要求
etymology: voc-(声音) + fer-(带来) + -ous(形容词后缀) = 带来巨大声音的，喧闹的
sentence_en: The policy change met with vociferous protests from student unions across the campus.
sentence_zh: 这项政策的改变遭到全校学生联合会的大声抗议和喧哗。

definition:
adj. 动荡不定的，易挥发的，反复无常的


搭配：volatile market 动荡不定的市场
etymology: volat-(飞) + -ile(易于…的) = 像鸟儿一样容易飞走的，易挥发、多变的
sentence_en: Investors should remain cautious when trading in a highly volatile stock market.
sentence_zh: 投资者在波动剧烈的股市中交易时应保持谨慎。

definition:
n. 意志，决心，自愿选择


搭配：of one's own volition 出于自愿
etymology: vol-(意志，愿望) + -ition(名词后缀) = 意志力的行为
sentence_en: The employee resigned from the company of his own volition, without any external pressure.
sentence_zh: 这名员工是出于自愿从公司辞职的，没有任何外部压力。

definition:
adj. 多卷的，大量的，庞大的（文件、书信等）


搭配：voluminous records 大量的档案
etymology: volumin-(卷，册) + -ous(形容词后缀) = 拥有许多卷的，庞大的
sentence_en: The investigators spent months analyzing the voluminous paperwork related to the financial fraud.
sentence_zh: 调查人员花了好几个月时间分析与这起金融诈骗案相关的浩繁文件。

definition:
adj. 贪婪的，狼吞虎咽的，贪得无厌的


搭配：voracious appetite 贪婪的胃口/求知欲
etymology: vor-(吞吃) + -acious(形容词后缀) = 拼命吞吃的，贪婪的
sentence_en: He is a voracious reader who can finish two thick novels over a single weekend.
sentence_zh: 他是一个博览群书的读者，一个周末就能读完两本厚厚的小说。

definition:
n. 漩涡，旋风，混乱的中心


搭配：vortex of conflict 冲突的漩涡
etymology: vert-(旋转) + -ex(名词后缀) = 旋转的流体，漩涡
sentence_en: The small boat was quickly sucked into the powerful vortex created by the cascading river.
sentence_zh: 小船很快被急流形成的强大漩涡吸了进去。

definition:
adj. 粗俗的，庸俗的，下流的


搭配：vulgar language 粗俗的语言
etymology: vulg-(平民大众) + -ar(形容词后缀) = 原指属于平民百姓的，后来引申为缺乏教养、粗俗的
sentence_en: The comedian was criticized for using vulgar humor during his television broadcast.
sentence_zh: 这位喜剧演员因在电视节目中开粗俗的玩笑而受到批评。

definition:
adj. 易受伤害的，脆弱的，易受攻击的


搭配：vulnerable group 弱势群体
etymology: vuln-(伤口，伤害) + -able(可…的) = 容易受伤的
sentence_en: Young seedlings are particularly vulnerable to sudden frosts during early spring.
sentence_zh: 幼苗在早春时节特别容易受到突发霜冻的伤害。

definition:
adj. 古怪的，荒唐的，滑稽的


搭配：wacky invention 古怪的发明
etymology: wack(模仿古怪行为) + -y(形容词后缀) = 行为怪异滑稽的
sentence_en: The scientist is famous for his wacky experiments and eccentric fashion style.
sentence_zh: 这位科学家以其古怪的实验和奇特的时尚风格而闻名。

definition:
v. 闲聊，废话，犹豫不决；n. 华夫饼


搭配：waffle on about 喋喋不休地谈论
etymology: waff(吠叫，胡言乱语) + -le(反复动作) = 废话连篇，犹豫不决
sentence_en: Instead of giving a direct answer, the politician began to waffle on about unrelated policies.
sentence_zh: 这位政治家没有直接回答，而是开始喋喋不休地谈论那些无关的政策。

definition:
adj. 谨慎的，机警的，提防的


搭配：be wary of 警惕…
etymology: war-(注意，警戒) + -y(形容词后缀) = 保持高度警觉的
sentence_en: Consumers should be wary of online advertisements promising overnight wealth.
sentence_zh: 消费者应当警惕那些承诺一夜暴富的网络广告。

definition:
v. 动摇，犹豫，颤抖


搭配：waver in determination 动摇决心
etymology: wave(波浪) + -er(反复动作) = 像波浪一样飘忽不定，动摇
sentence_en: Despite facing immense economic pressure, the company refused to waver from its core values.
sentence_zh: 尽管面临巨大的经济压力，该公司拒绝动摇其核心价值观。

definition:
v. （月亮）渐满，逐渐增大；n. 蜡


搭配：wax and wane 此消彼长，月圆月缺
etymology: wax(源自古英语，意为增大、成长)
sentence_en: Public interest in renewable energy tends to wax and wane depending on fluctuating oil prices.
sentence_zh: 公众对可再生能源的兴趣往往随着石油价格的波动而起伏不定。

definition:
adj. 任性的，桀骜不驯的，难管束的


搭配：wayward youth 不羁的青少年
etymology: way(路) + ward(向…方向) = 偏离正路的，任性固执的
sentence_en: The mentor dedicated his life to guiding wayward teenagers back onto the right path.
sentence_zh: 这位导师一生致力于引导那些误入歧途的青少年重回正轨。

definition:
v. 削弱，变弱


搭配：weaken the immune system 削弱免疫系统
etymology: weak(虚弱的) + -en(动词后缀，使…) = 使变弱
sentence_en: Prolonged exposure to pollution can significantly weaken human respiratory defenses.
sentence_zh: 长期暴露在污染环境中会显著削弱人体的呼吸防御能力。

definition:
adj. 疲倦的，厌倦的；v. 使疲劳


搭配：weary of 厌倦…
etymology: weary(源自日耳曼语族，意为筋疲力尽的)
sentence_en: Citizens grew increasingly weary of endless political scandals and corruption charges.
sentence_zh: 市民们对无休止的政治丑闻和贪腐指控越来越感到厌烦。

definition:
adj. 重大的，严肃的，沉重的


搭配：weighty matters 重大事务
etymology: weight(重量) + -y(形容词后缀) = 分量很重的，重大的
sentence_en: The conference focused on weighty issues such as global trade reform and poverty alleviation.
sentence_zh: 会议重点讨论了全球贸易改革和扶贫等重大问题。

definition:
v. 焊接，紧密结合


搭配：weld steel parts 焊接钢部件
etymology: weld(源自日耳曼语，原义指沸腾、熔接)
sentence_en: The manager successfully managed to weld diverse individuals into a high-performing team.
sentence_zh: 经理成功地将形形色色的人融合成一个高效的团队。

definition:
adj. 异想天开的，反复无常的，滑稽奇特的


搭配：whimsical design 异想天开的设计
etymology: whim(奇想，怪念头) + -ical(形容词后缀) = 充满奇思妙想的
sentence_en: The artist's sculptures are known for their whimsical shapes and vibrant colors.
sentence_zh: 这位艺术家的雕塑以其异想天开的造型和鲜艳的色彩而闻名。

definition:
adj. 健康的，有益身心的，合乎道德的


搭配：wholesome food 健康食品
etymology: whole(完整，健康) + -some(具有…倾向的) = 有利于身心完整的，健康的
sentence_en: The family-oriented film offered wholesome entertainment suitable for audiences of all ages.
sentence_zh: 这部合家欢电影提供了老少咸宜、有益身心的娱乐。

definition:
adj. 分布广泛的，普遍的


搭配：widespread concern 普遍关注
etymology: wide(宽广的) + spread(传播) = 在广阔范围内传播的，普遍的
sentence_en: The new safety regulations received widespread support from industry stakeholders.
sentence_zh: 新安全法规得到了业界利益相关者的广泛支持。

definition:
v. 行使（权力），挥舞（武器）


搭配：wield influence 发挥影响力
etymology: wield(源自古英语，意为掌控、统治)
sentence_en: Tech giants wield immense economic power in shaping global consumer habits.
sentence_zh: 科技巨头在塑造全球消费者习惯方面行使着巨大的经济权力。

definition:
n. 诡计，花言巧语，欺骗手段


搭配：wiles and tricks 诡计多端
etymology: wile(诡计，诱骗，同guile源流相关)
sentence_en: She managed to see through his charming wiles and refused to invest in the project.
sentence_zh: 她设法识破了他迷人的诡计，拒绝投资该项目。

definition:
v. 枯萎，凋谢，精疲力竭


搭配：wilt under the sun 在烈日下枯萎
etymology: wilt(源自日耳曼语系，意为干枯、下垂)
sentence_en: Without enough water during the heatwave, the indoor plants began to wilt rapidly.
sentence_zh: 在热浪期间如果没有足够的水分，室内的植物就会开始迅速枯萎。

definition:
adj. 狡猾的，诡计多端的


搭配：wily politician 狡猾的政客
etymology: wile(诡计) + -y(形容词后缀) = 满肚子诡计的
sentence_en: The wily detective managed to trap the suspect into a confession during the interrogation.
sentence_zh: 这位狡猾的侦探在审讯期间设法诱使嫌疑人招供。

definition:
v. 枯萎，凋谢，逐渐萎缩


搭配：wither away 枯萎消亡
etymology: wither(源自日耳曼语，指干瘪、风干)
sentence_en: Support for the controversial policy began to wither as economic losses mounted.
sentence_zh: 随着经济损失的累积，对这项备受争议的政策的支持开始逐渐减弱。

definition:
adj. 愚钝的，无知的，头脑简单的


搭配：witless remark 愚蠢的言论
etymology: wit(智慧，头脑) + -less(无，没有) = 没有头脑的，愚蠢的
sentence_en: He regretted making such a witless comment that offended his colleagues during the meeting.
sentence_zh: 他后悔在会上发表了那种冒犯同事的愚蠢言论。

definition:
adj. 风趣的，机智的


搭配：witty remark 机智的言论
etymology: wit(智慧，机智) + -y(形容词后缀) = 充满机智的
sentence_en: The speaker kept the audience entertained with his witty anecdotes and sharp observations.
sentence_zh: 演讲者以其风趣的轶事和敏锐的观察力让台下观众兴致盎然。

definition:
n. 巫术，法术，出神入化的造诣


搭配：technical wizardry 技术魔术/高超技术
etymology: wizard(男巫) + -ry(名词后缀，行业或技能) = 巫术，高超魔力
sentence_en: The film's visual effects are a piece of digital wizardry that stunned cinema-goers.
sentence_zh: 这部电影的视觉效果是一项令人惊叹的数字高超技术，让影迷叹为观止。

definition:
adj. 悲惨的，糟糕的，悲哀的


搭配：woeful inadequacy 极度的不足
etymology: woe(悲伤，痛苦) + -ful(充满…的) = 充满悲伤的，非常糟糕的
sentence_en: The remote village suffered from a woeful lack of basic medical infrastructure.
sentence_zh: 这个偏远村庄面临着严重缺乏基础医疗基础设施的困境。

definition:
adj. 奇妙的，令人惊叹的


搭配：wondrous landscape 奇妙的景观
etymology: wonder(奇观，惊奇) + -ous(形容词后缀) = 令人感到惊奇的
sentence_en: Scuba divers explored the wondrous coral reefs teeming with colorful marine life.
sentence_zh: 水肺潜水员探索了布满五颜六色海洋生物的神奇珊瑚礁。

definition:
adj. 习惯于，惯常的；n. 习惯，惯例


搭配：as is his wont 照例，像他一贯那样
etymology: wont(源自古英语，意为居住、习惯)
sentence_en: As was his wont, the professor arrived at the lecture hall ten minutes before the class started.
sentence_zh: 像往常一样，教授在课前十分钟到达了演讲厅。

definition:
adj. 世俗的，老于世故的，尘世的


搭配：worldly possessions 世俗财产
etymology: world(世界) + -ly(形容词后缀) = 属于世俗世界的，老练的
sentence_en: Having traveled to over fifty countries, she possessed a worldly perspective on international relations.
sentence_zh: 去过五十多个国家旅行的她，对国际关系有着老练世故的视角。

definition:
v. 争吵，争辩，口角；n. 争吵


搭配：legal wrangle 法律纠纷/诉讼争端
etymology: wrang-(争吵) + -le(反复动作) = 持续的争吵争辩
sentence_en: The two political parties engaged in a bitter budget wrangle that lasted for weeks.
sentence_zh: 这两个政党展开了持续数周的激烈预算争端。

definition:
n. 花环，花圈，圈状物


搭配：lay a wreath 敬献花圈
etymology: wreath(源自古英语，指扭曲、编织成圈之物)
sentence_en: Veterans gathered at the war memorial to lay a laurel wreath in honor of fallen soldiers.
sentence_zh: 退伍老兵聚集在战争纪念碑前，敬献月桂花环以纪念阵亡将士。

definition:
v. 猛扭，猛拉，使痛苦；n. 扳手，痛苦分离


搭配：wrench the ankle 扭伤脚踝
etymology: wrench(源自日耳曼语，原意为用力扭转)
sentence_en: It was a painful wrench for her to leave her hometown and move overseas.
sentence_zh: 离开家乡搬到海外对她来说是一次痛苦的分离。

definition:
v. 强夺，夺取，费力取得


搭配：wrest control 夺取控制权
etymology: wrest(源自古英语，意为用力扭扯、夺走)
sentence_en: Rebel forces managed to wrest control of the capital city after a fierce battle.
sentence_zh: 在经过一番激战后，反叛武装设法夺取了首都的控制权。

definition:
adj. 可怜的，悲惨的，恶劣的


搭配：wretched conditions 悲惨的条件
etymology: wretch(可怜的人) + -ed(形容词后缀) = 极其可怜悲惨的
sentence_en: Immigrants fleeing the war zone lived in wretched conditions in makeshift refugee camps.
sentence_zh: 逃离战区的移民在临时难民营里过着悲惨的生活。

definition:
n. 皱纹；v. 起皱，皱起


搭配：remove wrinkles 除皱
etymology: wrink-(起皱) + -le(小尺度反复动作) = 表面产生细小褶皱
sentence_en: She ironed her cotton shirt carefully to smooth out any stubborn wrinkles.
sentence_zh: 她仔细熨烫棉质衬衫，以抚平任何顽固的褶皱。

definition:
n. 令状，法律文书，法院传票


搭配：writ of habeas corpus 人身保护令
etymology: writ(源自古英语write，意为书面正式文件)
sentence_en: The defense lawyers filed a high court writ to halt the immediate deportation of the client.
sentence_zh: 辩护律师向高等法院提交了一份令状，以阻止对其当事人的立即驱逐出境。

definition:
adj. 苦笑的，歪曲的，讽刺的


搭配：wry smile 苦笑
etymology: wry(源自古英语，意为扭曲、偏斜)
sentence_en: He gave a wry smile when his computer crashed right before saving his final thesis.
sentence_zh: 当他的电脑在保存最终论文前崩溃时，他露出了苦笑。

definition:
n. 仇外，排外，恐外症


搭配：rise of xenophobia 仇外情绪的抬头
etymology: xeno-(陌生人，外国) + phobia(恐惧) = 对外国人和陌生人的极端恐惧与仇视
sentence_en: Economic downturns often trigger an increase in social tension and xenophobia.
sentence_zh: 经济下行往往会引发社会紧张局势和仇外情绪的加剧。

definition:
v. 复印；n. 静电复印件


搭配：xerox documents 复印文件
etymology: xero-(干) + -x(商标后缀，源自干法复印技术)
sentence_en: Please xerox these handout materials and distribute them to everyone in the conference room.
sentence_zh: 请把这些讲义材料复印一份，发给会议室里的每一个人。

definition:
v. 打哈欠；n. 哈欠


搭配：suppress a yawn 强忍哈欠
etymology: yawn(源自日耳曼语系，模拟张口呼吸动作)
sentence_en: The tedious lecture caused several students to yawn and lose concentration.
sentence_zh: 这场沉闷的讲座导致好几个学生打起了哈欠并且走神了。

definition:
v. 渴望，向往，思念


搭配：yearn for freedom 渴望自由
etymology: yearn(源自古英语，原指深切的情感渴望、痛苦思念)
sentence_en: After spending months working underground, the miners began to yearn for the warmth of the sun.
sentence_zh: 在地下工作了数月之后，矿工们开始渴望阳光的温暖。

definition:
n. 酵母，发酵粉


搭配：brewer's yeast 啤酒酵母
etymology: yeast(源自日耳曼语，与沸腾、起泡相关)
sentence_en: Bakers use yeast to make dough rise before baking it into bread.
sentence_zh: 面包师使用酵母让面团在烤成面包之前发酵膨胀。

definition:
n. 瘾，强烈的渴望；日元（日本货币）


搭配：have a yen for travel 渴望旅游
etymology: yen(源自汉语“愿”在粤语或方言中的发音演变，意为渴望)
sentence_en: She suddenly developed a strong yen for Japanese cuisine after watching a cooking show.
sentence_zh: 在看了一档烹饪节目后，她突然产生了一种对日本料理的强烈渴望。

definition:
v. 产出，产生，屈服；n. 产量，收益


搭配：crop yield 作物产量
etymology: yield(源自古英语，原意为支付、回报、交出)
sentence_en: Advanced irrigation technologies can significantly increase agricultural crop yields in dry regions.
sentence_zh: 先进的灌溉技术可以显著提高干旱地区的农作物产量。

definition:
n. 轭，束缚，枷锁；v. 束缚，连接


搭配：under the yoke of 在…的奴役/束缚下
etymology: yoke(源自印欧语根，意为连接、套上牛轭)
sentence_en: The revolution successfully freed the nation from the yoke of colonial oppression.
sentence_zh: 这场革命成功地使国家摆脱了殖民压迫的枷锁。

definition:
n. 乡巴佬，粗俗的乡下人


搭配：local yokel 当地乡下人
etymology: yokel(源自方言，指乡间干粗活的农夫)
sentence_en: The city slicker looked down on the countryfolk, mocking them as uneducated yokels.
sentence_zh: 这个城里人瞧不起乡下人，嘲笑他们是没受过教育的乡巴佬。

definition:
n. 热情，热忱，热心


搭配：zeal for learning 学习的热情
etymology: zeal(源自希腊语zelos，意为狂热、激情)
sentence_en: The young activist approached environmental reform with boundless zeal and dedication.
sentence_zh: 这位年轻的活动家以无限的热忱和奉献精神投身于环保改革。

definition:
n. 狂热者，盲信者，极端分子


搭配：religious zealot 宗教狂热分子
etymology: zeal(热情) + -ot(名词后缀，指人) = 充满狂热偏执的人
sentence_en: Religious zealots often reject any form of compromise or rational dialogue.
sentence_zh: 宗教狂热分子往往拒绝任何形式的妥协或理性对话。

definition:
adj. 热情的，狂热的，积极的


搭配：zealous supporter 狂热的支持者
etymology: zeal(热情) + -ous(形容词后缀) = 满腔热忱的
sentence_en: The candidate's zealous supporters campaigned tirelessly across the entire state.
sentence_zh: 这位候选人的狂热支持者在整个州不辞劳苦地展开竞选活动。

definition:
n. 天顶，最高点，鼎盛时期


搭配：reach the zenith 达到鼎盛时期
etymology: zenith(源自阿拉伯语，意为头顶方向的天顶)
sentence_en: The Roman Empire reached its territorial zenith during the reign of Emperor Trajan.
sentence_zh: 罗马帝国在图拉真皇帝统治时期达到了其领土扩张的顶峰。

definition:
n. 西风，和风，微风


搭配：gentle zephyr 轻柔的微风
etymology: Zephyrus(希腊神话中的西风之神) = 和风，西风
sentence_en: A cool zephyr blew across the valley, bringing relief from the afternoon heat.
sentence_zh: 阵阵凉爽的西风吹过山谷，驱散了午后的暑气。

definition:
n. 热情，兴致，风味（柠檬皮等的香味）


搭配：zest for life 对生活的热情
etymology: zest(源自法语，指橙皮或柠檬皮用来调味的刮屑，引申为风味、兴致)
sentence_en: Despite her eighty years, she approaches everyday tasks with an infectious zest for life.
sentence_zh: 尽管已经八十高龄，她对待日常事务仍有着极具感染力的生活热情。

definition:
n. 之字形；adj. 之字形的；v. 曲折前行


搭配：zigzag path 之字形小路
etymology: zigzag(拟声叠词，模拟来回拐弯的形状)
sentence_en: The hiking trail led us in a steep zigzag pattern up the rocky mountain slope.
sentence_zh: 这条徒步小径呈陡峭的之字形引领我们登上多石的山坡。

definition:
n. 无数，极大的数量（非正式）


搭配：a zillion times 无数次
etymology: million(百万) + 模仿发音构成的虚构极大数字后缀
sentence_en: I have told you a zillion times not to leave your keys on the kitchen counter.
sentence_zh: 我已经跟你说过无数次了，不要把钥匙留在厨房柜台上。

definition:
n. 地带，地区，区域；v. 划分成带


搭配：time zone 时区
etymology: zone(源自希腊语zone，意为腰带、环带区域)
sentence_en: The city government designated this industrial sector as a low-emission environmental zone.
sentence_zh: 市政府将这个工业区指定为低碳环保区。

definition:
n. 分区规划，区域划分（城市规划法）


搭配：zoning laws 分区法规
etymology: zone(区域) + -ing(名词后缀，行为) = 划定区域的规划
sentence_en: Strict zoning laws prevent heavy manufacturing factories from operating near residential neighborhoods.
sentence_zh: 严格的分区法规防止重工业工厂在居民区附近运营。

definition:
n. 动物学


搭配：department of zoology 动物学系
etymology: zoo-(动物) + -logy(…学) = 研究动物的科学，动物学
sentence_en: She enrolled in a comprehensive zoology course to study animal behavior and physiology.
sentence_zh: 她选修了一门全面的动物学课程，以研究动物的行为和生理学。

definition:
v. 激增，急速上升，轰鸣驶过，焦距变焦


搭配：zoom in 放大，聚焦
etymology: zoom(拟声词，模仿飞机疾驶而过的嗡嗡声或快速拉近镜头的声音)
sentence_en: House prices in the metropolitan area continue to zoom upward despite rising mortgage rates.
sentence_zh: 尽管抵押贷款利率在上升，大都市地区的房价仍在继续飙升。

definition:
n. 小夏南瓜，西葫芦


搭配：grilled zucchini 烤西葫芦
etymology: zucchini(源自意大利语zucca南瓜的指小词)
sentence_en: The chef sliced the fresh zucchini and tossed it into the Mediterranean vegetable stew.
sentence_zh: 厨师将新鲜的西葫芦切片，扔进了地中海蔬菜炖汤中。

definition:
n. 受精卵，合子


搭配：zygote development 受精卵发育
etymology: zygotos(结合在一起的) = 卵子和精子结合形成的受精卵
sentence_en: In sexual reproduction, a single-celled zygote is formed by the fusion of a sperm and an egg.
sentence_zh: 在有性生殖中，单细胞受精卵是由精子和卵子结合形成的。

definition:
n./v. 尊敬，崇敬，敬畏
搭配：show profound reverence
etymology: re-(加强) + ver(敬畏) + ence = 满怀深深的敬畏 = 崇敬
sentence_en: The native community holds a profound reverence for the ancient burial grounds.
sentence_zh: 当地社区对这片古老的墓地怀有深深的崇敬。

definition:
n. 修辞学，华丽的辞藻，雄辩术
搭配：empty political rhetoric
etymology: 源自希腊语 rhetor (演说家) = 演说家的语言技巧 = 雄辩术/华丽辞藻
sentence_en: The speaker's empty rhetoric failed to convince the skeptical academic audience.
sentence_zh: 演讲者空洞的华丽辞藻未能说服持怀疑态度的学术听众。

definition:
v. 仔细检查，彻底审查，细看
搭配：scrutinize financial records
etymology: 源自 scrutiny (仔细检查) 的动词形式 = 像打着手电筒翻找废墟一样看个明白 = 彻底审查
sentence_en: Security analysts constantly scrutinize network server traffic to block automated hacks.
sentence_zh: 安全分析师不断仔细审查网络服务器流量，以拦截自动化的黑客攻击。

definition:
adj. 随后的，后来的，并发的
搭配：subsequent developments
etymology: sub-(在...下面/紧随) + sequ(跟随) + ent = 紧跟在屁股后面的 = 随后的
sentence_en: Initial laboratory tests were ambiguous, but subsequent experiments confirmed the theory.
sentence_zh: 最初的实验室测试模棱两可，但随后的实验证实了该理论。

definition:
v. 颠覆，推推翻（传统、政权等），暗中破坏
搭配：subvert traditional values
etymology: sub-(在下方) + vert(转动) = 从地基底下开始锄土转动 = 颠覆/暗中破坏
sentence_en: The newly released software platform directly attempts to subvert traditional retail models.
sentence_zh: 新发布的软件平台直接企图颠覆传统的零售模式。

definition:
adj. 易受影响的，脆弱的，易受感染的
搭配：be susceptible to infection
etymology: sub-(在下面) + cept(拿/接) + ible = 极易在底下被别人拿捏或接招的 = 易受影响的
sentence_en: Young children and elderly patients are highly susceptible to seasonal respiratory illnesses.
sentence_zh: 幼儿和老年患者极易感染季节性呼吸道疾病。

definition:
adj. 空前的，史无前例的（托福高分常客）
搭配：unprecedented economic growth
etymology: un-(无) + precedent(先例) + ed = 历史翻烂了都找不到第二个的 = 空前的
sentence_en: The rapid development of machine learning created an unprecedented velocity of data growth.
sentence_zh: 机器学习的迅速发展创造了前所未有的数据增长速度。

definition:
v. 解开（谜团），阐明，拆散，瓦解
搭配：unravel a complex mystery
etymology: un-(解开) + ravel(缠绕) = 把死死绞在一块的乱绳理顺 = 解开谜团
sentence_en: Forensic computer experts spent weeks trying to unravel the complex malware source code.
sentence_zh: 法医计算机专家花了几周时间试图解开复杂的恶意软件源代码。
